---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API to send messages, reply in threads, list channels and users, read channel history, create channels, and upload files. Use when Gemini CLI needs to perform Slack workspace operations such as posting a message to a channel, responding in a thread, reading conversation history, resolving channel or user info, creating a channel, or uploading a file to Slack.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

This skill provides dependency-free Node.js scripts for common Slack Web API operations. Every script reads a bot token from the `SLACK_TOKEN` environment variable and prints concise, LLM-friendly `Success:`/`Failure:` output, exiting non-zero on failure.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18+ (scripts use native `fetch`, `FormData`, and `Blob`; no npm packages required).
- A Slack bot token exported as `SLACK_TOKEN`, e.g. `export SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-...`.
- Required OAuth scopes depend on the operation; see `references/api.md` for the full scope table.

## Quick Start

Send a message to a channel:

```bash
node scripts/send_message.cjs #general "Hello from the agent"
```

List channels to find a channel ID:

```bash
node scripts/list_channels.cjs --limit 20
```

## Sending Messages

Use `scripts/send_message.cjs <channel> "<text>" [--thread <ts>]`.

- `<channel>`: channel ID (`C...`) or name (`#general`). IDs are more reliable, especially for private channels.
- Text supports Slack `mrkdwn` formatting: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `<https://example.com|label>`, `<@U123>` mentions, `<#C123|name>` channel links.
- Add `--thread <ts>` to reply in a thread (pass the parent message's `ts` value as a string).

## Reading Messages

Use `scripts/read_history.cjs <channel> [--limit N] [--oldest TS] [--latest TS] [--cursor C]`.

- Returns newest-first messages with `ts`, sender, and truncated text; thread reply counts are shown when present.
- `ts` values look like `1712345678.000100` — always treat them as strings, never floats.

## Channels

- `scripts/list_channels.cjs [--limit N] [--cursor C] [--types T]` — list public/private channels the bot can see, with pagination. When output is truncated, the script prints the `next_cursor` to continue.
- `scripts/create_channel.cjs <name> [--private]` — create a channel (requires `channels:manage`).

## Users

Use `scripts/list_users.cjs [--limit N] [--cursor C]` to list workspace members (id, name, bot flag).

## Files

Use `scripts/upload_file.cjs <channel> <filepath> [--title T] [--comment C]` to upload a file (requires `files:write`).

## Conventions

- Prefer channel/user IDs (`C...`, `U...`) over names when an ID is already known; resolve names via `list_channels.cjs` / `list_users.cjs`.
- All scripts truncate long output (e.g., message text) to keep responses context-friendly.
- On API errors, scripts print `Failure: <slack_error>` and exit 1. Do not retry blindly; see `references/api.md` for rate limits and error handling.

## Reference

See `references/api.md` for authentication, scopes, pagination, rate limits, message formatting, and error codes.

# Slack API Reference

## Authentication

- All scripts require `SLACK_TOKEN` (a bot token starting with `xoxb-`).
- Bot tokens act as the bot user; the bot must be a member of a channel to read it or send messages in it (invite the bot to the channel first).
- Scopes are granted when the app is installed. A missing scope returns `missing_scope`.

## Scopes

| Script | Endpoint used | Required scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| send_message.cjs | chat.postMessage | chat:write |
| read_history.cjs | conversations.history | channels:history |
| list_channels.cjs | conversations.list | channels:read |
| create_channel.cjs | conversations.create | channels:manage |
| list_users.cjs | users.list | users:read |
| upload_file.cjs | files.upload | files:write |

## Endpoints

| Method | Endpoint | Key params |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST | chat.postMessage | channel, text, thread_ts |
| GET | conversations.list | types, limit, cursor |
| GET | conversations.history | channel, limit, oldest, latest, cursor |
| POST | conversations.create | name, is_private |
| GET | users.list | limit, cursor |
| POST | files.upload | channels, file, title, initial_comment |

## Pagination

- Slack paginates with `limit` (max 999 for conversations) and `cursor`.
- The next page cursor is in `response_metadata.next_cursor`; an empty string means no more pages.
- `list_channels.cjs`, `list_users.cjs`, and `read_history.cjs` print the `next_cursor` when more results exist.

## Rate Limits

- Slack rate limits per method tier; Tier 3 (most conversation methods) allows about 1 request per second per token.
- A `429` response includes a `Retry-After` header (seconds). Back off for that duration before retrying.
- For bulk operations, add a small delay between calls.

## Message Formatting

- mrkdwn: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `<https://example.com|label>` links, `<@U123>` user mentions, `<#C123|name>` channel links.
- For rich layouts (buttons, headers, etc.) use `blocks` JSON via chat.postMessage; the send script accepts plain text, so convert to blocks when the user needs rich layouts.

## Threads

- Reply in a thread by passing the parent message's `ts` as `thread_ts`. `ts` is a string like `1712345678.000100`; never parse it as a float.
- `conversations.history` returns thread replies only when `thread_ts` is provided.

## Error Handling

- Every response has `ok: true|false`; errors include an `error` code.
- Common codes:
  - `not_authed` / `invalid_auth` — bad token
  - `missing_scope` — token lacks the required scope
  - `channel_not_found` — bad channel ID/name
  - `not_in_channel` — bot is not a member
  - `is_archived` — channel is archived
  - `name_taken` — channel name already exists
  - `rate_limited` — slow down (see Rate Limits)
- All skill scripts print `Failure: <code>` and exit 1 on API errors.

## Gotchas

- Channel names are lowercased by Slack and cannot contain spaces.
- `conversations.list` with `types=private_channel` only returns private channels the bot belongs to.
- `users.list` includes bots; filter with `is_bot`.
- Uploaded files appear in the channel as a message from the bot.
